raw_response:
I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation that fits Quzhou County best. I am 65, so I will not chase labor-intensive or risky cash crops. I want something I know well, that matches local machinery, local water conditions, and local buyers. So on my main land I will finish the winter wheat that is already in the ground, then after harvest I will plant summer maize right away. I will use improved or hybrid seed, control fertilizer instead of pushing it too hard, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what is needed. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is familiar, practical, and easier for me to manage than deep ploughing every season. My goal is steady yield, lower labor pressure, and less production risk.
